planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, humus-rich, acid to neutral soil in an open but sheltered site; site 'Aurora' where its large, bronze-shaded yellow flowers can be seen from indoors during its midwinter to late-winter bloom.

This vigorous, spreading RHS Award of Garden Merit selection carries the largest individual flowers of any witch hazel cultivar, with crimped yellow petals shaded bronze-red toward the base and a sweet, carrying fragrance. Broadly oval leaves turn clear yellow in fall. Avoid exposed windy sites and shallow chalky soils that dry out quickly, since the fibrous root system resents drought.

planting.note: Plant in fall or spring in organically rich, moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; the comparatively narrow, upright-vase habit makes 'Orange Peel' a good fit for smaller gardens and foundation plantings where a typical wide-spreading witch hazel would not fit.

directions: Plant in fall or spring in organically rich, moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; the comparatively narrow, upright-vase habit makes 'Orange Peel' a good fit for smaller gardens and foundation plantings where a typical wide-spreading witch hazel would not fit. Introduced by Kalmthout Arboretum in Belgium in 1988, it is one of the truest orange-flowered witch hazels, with sweetly fragrant, crimped, strap-shaped petals set off by a dark purple calyx and opening early to mid-winter. Dark green oval leaves turn yellow, orange, and red in fall, adding a second season of color. Give it consistent moisture and avoid waterlogged or drought-prone sites, since the shallow root system is sensitive to both extremes.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in humus-rich, moist, well-drained, acid to neutral soil in an open, sheltered site; because 'Jermyns Gold' forms a large, erect shrub over time, give it plenty of room away from paths and structures from the start.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in humus-rich, moist, well-drained, acid to neutral soil in an open, sheltered site; because 'Jermyns Gold' forms a large, erect shrub over time, give it plenty of room away from paths and structures from the start. Named by Hillier Nurseries in 2000 for the National Collection of Hamamelis grown along Jermyns Lane at Sir Harold Hillier Gardens, this RHS Award of Garden Merit selection of Chinese witch hazel produces richly fragrant, golden-yellow ribbon petals lightly tinted red at the base in mid to late winter. Its upright, vigorous habit distinguishes it from the more spreading mollis selections. Fall foliage turns soft butter-yellow before leaf drop.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in acid to neutral, humus-rich, well-drained soil in an open, sunny spot sheltered from strong wind; 'Goldcrest' matures into a large broad shrub, so allow generous space from the outset.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in acid to neutral, humus-rich, well-drained soil in an open, sunny spot sheltered from strong wind; 'Goldcrest' matures into a large broad shrub, so allow generous space from the outset. This RHS Award of Garden Merit Chinese witch hazel selection carries deep golden-yellow, ribbon-like petals distinctly tinged claret-red at the base, opening on bare branches in late winter with an intense, sweet fragrance among the strongest of any witch hazel. Broad, downy-backed leaves turn yellow and orange in fall. Its size makes it best suited to larger borders or woodland-edge plantings rather than small gardens.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moderately fertile, moist, well-drained, neutral to acid soil in an open but sheltered site; 'Birgit' blooms later, in February and March, so pair it with earlier cultivars to extend the witch hazel display.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moderately fertile, moist, well-drained, neutral to acid soil in an open but sheltered site; 'Birgit' blooms later, in February and March, so pair it with earlier cultivars to extend the witch hazel display. Regarded as one of the darkest red-flowered witch hazels available, it carries dark red sepals behind narrow, crinkled reddish-pink petals with a mild fragrance, on a rounded to spreading shrub. New spring growth emerges bronze-flushed before maturing to mid green, then turning butter-yellow suffused with orange-red in fall. Tolerates deep, humus-rich soils over chalk but performs best where soil stays evenly moist.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in cool, acid to neutral, humus-rich soil; because 'Zuccariniana' is the last witch hazel to flower each year, place it where its pale late-winter blooms will follow, rather than compete with, earlier-flowering cultivars.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in cool, acid to neutral, humus-rich soil; because 'Zuccariniana' is the last witch hazel to flower each year, place it where its pale late-winter blooms will follow, rather than compete with, earlier-flowering cultivars. This distinctive Japanese witch hazel selection extends the witch hazel season into late February and March with slender, pale lemon-yellow petals set against small, dark brown, incurved sepals and a light fragrance. It slowly develops an upright trunk topped by a broad, spreading crown, and its bronze-tinted spring foliage matures to dark green before coloring coppery orange and red in autumn. Cold winters actually enhance flowering, making it well suited to northern gardens.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moderately fertile, moist, well-drained, acid to neutral soil in an open but not exposed site; because 'Carmine Red' spreads wider than it grows tall, give it more lateral room than most upright witch hazel cultivars.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moderately fertile, moist, well-drained, acid to neutral soil in an open but not exposed site; because 'Carmine Red' spreads wider than it grows tall, give it more lateral room than most upright witch hazel cultivars. Originating at Hillier Nurseries, this vigorous, spreading selection bears clusters of large, slightly fragrant, dark pinkish-red crimped petals on bare winter branches, among the strongest reds in the genus. Glossy green summer leaves turn a clear yellow in fall, and the winter flowers draw early-foraging bees on mild days. Tolerant of deer browse pressure better than many other flowering shrubs.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic to neutral soil in full sun to part shade; because 'Early Bright' opens roughly two weeks ahead of typical Chinese witch hazels, site it where its early color can be seen through a window during the coldest weeks of winter.

directions: Plant container shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, acidic to neutral soil in full sun to part shade; because 'Early Bright' opens roughly two weeks ahead of typical Chinese witch hazels, site it where its early color can be seen through a window during the coldest weeks of winter. Selected at the Scott Arboretum of Swarthmore College after staff noticed a seedling that consistently bloomed earlier than its neighbors, it was introduced in 1988 and named for its precociously early, golden-yellow, ribbon-shaped petals tinted red at the base. The vase-shaped, upright shrub carries a strong sweet fragrance, and its spidery flowers curl closed to protect themselves during hard freezes before reopening on milder days. A reliable choice for gardeners who want the earliest possible start to the witch hazel season.
